problem: Stale recovery permits multiple concurrent recovery claims for one opportunity, causing duplicate takeover attempts and coordination churn even when product mutation is later avoided.
acceptance: Two or more concurrent recovery attempts for the same opportunity yield exactly one active recovery claimant.
Losers preserve collision evidence and perform no substantive target mutation.
Late original or recovery returns remain reconcilable append-only evidence.
No Current, Human Accepted, Served, or queue authority promotion occurs.
title: Atomic recovery-claim dedup canary
mission: Implement and verify host-level create-if-absent uniqueness for stale-recovery takeover so one opportunity can have at most one active recovery claimant at a time, while preserving losing collision evidence, late returns, original lineage and all authority boundaries. Reuse the existing recovery protocol and discovery/claim atomicity patterns rather than adding a second scheduler.

incident_repair.reason: Page Thread recovery produced multiple concurrent takeover attempts for one opportunity; later workers had to stop or supersede duplicate recovery after detecting the qualifying pair.

human_friction_reduction.reason: A unique active recovery claimant reduces coordination churn without asking the human to choose among competing recovery chats.

regression_prevention.reason: The current stale protocol preserves append-only evidence but concurrent recovery claims can still race; a host-level uniqueness canary tests the missing collision boundary directly.

unblock_value.reason: Mass /wc recovery is now exercising stale lanes across surface and GEN2 work; preventing recovery stampedes protects useful throughput as parallelism rises.

falsification: If current host-level recovery claiming already proves exactly-one active claimant under true concurrent repository writes, with losers unable to overwrite and with late returns preserved, this proposal should be closed as duplicate/no-op rather than implemented.
